subject.title: Browser backend plugin interface (support third-party drivers via MCP/custom adapter)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser backend registration API for third-party drivers, and what permission/config/security contract should that API require?
rationale: The code change would create a new public Plugin SDK and config surface for browser control, where a bad adapter can drive signed-in browser state or remote CDP endpoints; automation cannot choose that boundary safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add guarded backend registry
options.body: Create a versioned Plugin SDK backend contract with manifest permissions, registered driver ids, config/schema/doctor integration, runtime dispatch, docs, and security tests.

options.title: Keep replacement-only plugins
options.body: Document that third-party browser engines must disable the bundled browser plugin and provide a whole replacement browser tool, avoiding a new core driver registry.

options.title: Handle service drivers case by case
options.body: Continue landing service- or topology-specific built-in drivers such as Browserbase or extension relay work without committing to a generic third-party adapter API.

recommendation.title: Add guarded backend registry
recommendation.body: Create a versioned Plugin SDK backend contract with manifest permissions, registered driver ids, config/schema/doctor integration, runtime dispatch, docs, and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the browser driver restoration, browser plugin ownership, and plugin-boundary refactors relevant to this design choice.
